players.product: trapped-ion quantum computers (Forte, Forte Enterprise) sold as systems and as cloud access, plus quantum networking, sensing and security products

quarterly_data.signal: IonQ 10-K: 2025 revenue was $130,016 thousand, up 202% from $43,073 thousand - quantum hardware $69,946 thousand and platform, consulting and support services $60,070 thousand; by customer location United States $86,957 thousand, Switzerland $16,630 thousand and other international $26,429 thousand. Approximately $370.0 million of revenue is expected from remaining performance obligations, about 40% within the next twelve months; net loss attributable to IonQ was $510.4 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $130,016 thousand (+202%); quantum hardware $69,946 thousand; RPO approximately $370.0 million (40% within 12 months)

quarterly_data.signal: IonQ 10-K: IonQ acquired Capella (July 11, 2025) and Oxford Ionics (September 16, 2025) in 2025, alongside Vector Atomic and others, and Skyloom in January 2026; on January 25, 2026 it agreed to acquire SkyWater Technology, a U.S.-based semiconductor foundry, which IonQ believes will accelerate its roadmap by providing embedded access to a secure quantum foundry. Its customers, potential customers and partners include the United States Air Force Research Lab, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency and Oak Ridge National Laboratory.
quarterly_data.figure: Capella July 11, 2025; Oxford Ionics September 16, 2025; SkyWater agreement January 25, 2026

quarterly_data.signal: IonQ 10-K: in November 2025 IonQ entered a strategic collaboration agreement and master research agreement with the University of Chicago (IP license and building naming rights in exchange for 2,108,993 IonQ shares, with a research prepayment valued at $68.7 million) and a commercial agreement for the sale of quantum computing hardware and services, from which it recognized $1.8 million of revenue in 2025.
